title: Indic LaunchKit
tagline: From app to launch. Beautifully prepared.
short_description: An open-source, offline studio for Android release artwork, APK inspection, and checksummed release packs—with a standalone CLI for AI agents.
full_description: Turn your real app icon and screenshots into a consistent release presentation. Indic LaunchKit combines a native desktop studio with a separate command-line tool, both powered by the same Rust engine.

Create a portable project, import local assets, edit captions, choose Aurora, Paper, or Midnight, and preview the actual rendered result. Export a 512px icon, 1024 × 500 feature graphic, 1200 × 630 social card, and 1080 × 1920 screenshot artwork without an account or a cloud service.

Optionally inspect an APK to read its literal package, version, SDK requirements, size, and SHA-256. Exported packs include product metadata, a review checklist, and checksums. Copying the APK into a pack is optional.

The separate launchkit CLI supports explicit arguments, versioned JSON responses, validation, headless previews, and dry-run export planning. It is suitable for repeatable scripts and AI-agent workflows without opening a desktop window.

This is an unsigned public beta. Native build and CLI test evidence is supplied for each released platform; interactive desktop integration was checked on Windows. APK signatures, store acceptance, legal documents, code signing, and automatic publishing are outside this release.

platforms.requirements: Windows 10/11 x64. Desktop requires Edge WebView2. The separate CLI archive needs Microsoft Visual C++ v14 x64 runtime, but no WebView. Unsigned beta.
x64 desktop with WebKitGTK 4.1. Built on Ubuntu 22.04; native desktop packages and a separate CLI archive. Graphical session required only for the desktop app.
Apple Silicon, macOS 12+ desktop target. No Developer ID signing or notarization. Native builds and CLI checks run on macOS 15; interactive macOS GUI testing is not claimed.

faqs.question: Can an AI agent use LaunchKit without a desktop?
faqs.answer: Yes. Download the separate CLI archive and use launchkit with --json. It supports project creation, asset import, APK inspection, validation, preview, schema inspection, and dry-run exports. It never uploads or publishes anything.

faqs.question: Does it sign APKs or publish to stores?
faqs.answer: No. It prepares artwork, metadata, checksums and a checklist. Signing, complete store listings, privacy policy review and publication remain separate steps.

faqs.question: Does LaunchKit upload my files?
faqs.answer: The application has no account, analytics or upload service. Selected files are copied to the project folder and processed locally. You choose where exports go.

faqs.question: Can I use and modify it commercially?
faqs.answer: The project source is MIT licensed. Bundled fonts retain SIL OFL 1.1 and dependencies retain their licenses. The IndicStudio name does not imply endorsement of modified distributions.

faqs.question: Which languages and images are supported?
faqs.answer: PNG, JPEG and WebP images are supported within documented size limits. Bundled fonts cover Latin and Devanagari; unsupported characters and text that exceeds template limits produce explicit errors.

privacy_summary: Local processing with no application accounts, analytics, or uploads. You control project files, imported copies and exports.
release_note: Unsigned beta: Windows Authenticode and Apple Developer ID/notarization are not configured. Check the release receipts and SHA-256 values. Desktop integration was checked on Windows; Linux/macOS native builds and CLI checks do not establish interactive GUI usability.
